standard_prerequisites.name: Equivalence between sheaves of sets and Galois sets
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the given sheaf into a G-set whose invariants compute the global sections.

standard_prerequisites.name: Sheaves represented by objects of the site
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the global sections with morphisms from the sheaf represented by the site's final object.

core_obligations: Formal computation (proof lines 8678-8694): the author identifies the global sections with morphisms from the sheaf represented by the spectrum of K, then, through the equivalence of the cited theorem, with G-equivariant maps from a point to the corresponding G-set, and hence with the invariants of that G-set; each identification is attributed.

Direct proof (proof lines 8694-8729): a global section gives a G-invariant element of the stalk, and conversely an invariant element of the stalk is shown to glue to a global section, using the equivalence of the cited theorem and its compatibility with the action.
proof_roadmap: Use the equivalence between sheaves and Galois sets to express global sections as equivariant maps out of a point.
Identify those with the invariants of the stalk.
Give a second, direct proof by producing a global section from an invariant stalk element.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the global sections of a sheaf on the small etale site of the spectrum of a field as the invariants, under the absolute Galois group, of its stalk at a fixed geometric point (statement lines 8667-8675). The proof contains two complete arguments: a formal chain of identifications through the equivalence between sheaves of sets and Galois sets, with each step attributed (proof lines 8678-8694), and a direct argument constructing a global section from an invariant element of the stalk (proof lines 8694-8729). The non-formal content is the compatibility of the equivalence with the group action. The claim is H2: two parallel arguments, the second written out in detail.
